youtube.title: Why America Gave Up the Stick Shift (Europe Didn't)
youtube.description:
Fewer than 2 in every 100 new American cars have a clutch pedal, yet most new cars in Europe still did until recently. It wasn't laziness. A $57 GM option in 1940, 27-cent gasoline that hid the early automatic's thirst, and US driving tests that never tell manual from automatic did it, while Europe's fuel taxes and automatic-only licences kept the stick alive for decades. Sources: EPA Automotive Trends Report; GM Heritage Center; GOV.UK. The Hidden Why: the real reason behind the everyday things you use.
#TheHiddenWhy #facts #explained
